Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Riverton WY
915 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Scattered snow showers continue tonight, mainly across
  northern and western portions of the area. Brief heavy snow
  and reduced visibilities will remain threats with these 
  showers overnight.

- Unsettled conditions and cooler temperatures continue over the
  weekend into early next week feeling more like winter going
  towards the end of November. 

- A bit of a warmup for Tuesday and Wednesday with the next
  system to start pushing in for Thanksgiving and beyond but
  more of a west of the Divide impact due to zonal westerly flow
  aloft.

&&

.UPDATE...
Issued at 1223 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

One wave of snow showers continues to sweep east currently,
after having produced a couple inches of snow along the I-80
corridor. Some convective activity is building in around the
central circulation across Fremont and Natrona Counties, which
has sparked a few new snow showers here at the office. This area
should be exiting to the northeast quickly, so any showers will
be a rain/snow mix and produce just a skiff of snow at best. The
next area of precip is stretched across the Idaho/Utah border,
and will be stretching to the northeast into the western 
mountains later today and tonight. This will be the last round 
of snowfall as the whole system moves northeast. There is still 
enough snow production expected through this evening to keep the
Winter Weather Advisory in effect through its expiration at 
11PM tonight.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1230 AM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

IR currently depicts ample cloud coverage across the entire CWA
with cold cloud tops pushing around the upper level trough to
the east. This is where the strongest PVA anomalies are located
coming out of northeastern Utah into parts of Wyoming that will
continue into Friday morning. The main finger of the PFJ
continues to deepen the aforementioned trough with the 130kt jet
max pushing into its base near central California into southern
Nevada. This is allowing for the trough to dig further south
with more major impacts to be had for Colorado. Minor impacts
still expected for the CWA, mainly for western mountains with
decent accumulations. Radar shows the spreading of snow in from
the southwest and will continue for much of Friday as well. 

Immediate minor concerns will be for eastern Sweetwater to
southern Natrona counties where ongoing light snow is making way
for slick roadways and reduced visibilities for the I-80 and Hwy
287 corridors. This is mainly for points east of Rock Springs
and Jeffrey City until at least mid Friday morning. A bit more
breezy as well for this area of the wind corridor that will help
to aid in these impacts, especially that of the Friday morning
commute. Otherwise, western mountain snow continues overnight
with the highest snowfall rates not expected until the afternoon
hours that will impact evening commutes over western passes to
include Teton/Togwotee and extending now to South Pass that has
been added to the winter weather advisory through late Friday
night. Pass level elevations will look at 2 to 5 inches of
accumulations (60-80%), higher for western passes. Lower valleys
are looking at 1 to 2 inches at best with lower confidence
(20-30%). As the system becomes more open and progressive with
its eastward progression, it will pivot to the east of the
Divide that will extend mountain snow to the Bighorns dropping
to parts of Natrona and Johnson Counties into Friday evening and
overnight lingering through Saturday morning. Bighorn mountain
passes are looking at 2 to 4 inches of accumulation (30-40%) for
Friday night and lower elevations to the east 1 to 2 inches.
Gusty winds will be the aid that could result in needed hazards
later on but holding off with BYZ to include northern Johnson
along with their Sheridan County. Otherwise, any snow into the
Wind River and Bighorn Basins will be limited in accumulation
and for far eastern portions of these areas not expecting any
impacts at this time.

The main cold front will finally push through during Friday
afternoon and into the evening allowing for a bit colder air to
ooze into the CWA for the weekend to be more seasonable to just
below average for this time of year. Areas east of the Divide 
will struggle to reach 40 degrees in the afternoon with 
overnight lows down into the teens. The PFJ continues to remain 
south of the state through Monday to keep the colder 
temperatures with minor chances for higher elevation snow at 
times during this time but limited in impact and mainly for 
areas like Yellowstone and higher western mountains. Mountain 
passes will stay mainly dry for the most part as the PFJ 
retreats north by Tuesday with induced ridging through late 
Wednesday ahead of the next possible storm system Thanksgiving 
and beyond. It is looking more as an impact west of the Divide 
with mountain snow and much lighter accumulation for the 
valleys being a more zonal west flow off the Pacific. 
Temperatures not as cold more seasonable to just above average 
through the end of the week and into the following weekend. 
Details unknown at this time but stay tuned for details in the 
coming days.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 914 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

The current weather system continues to bring snow chances to the 
area through Saturday afternoon. Snow will be showery and result in 
brief IFR to LIFR conditions in the heaviest showers. Generally
conditions will be MVFR to VFR outside of snow showers and MVFR
to IFR during snow showers. Due to the showery nature of the 
snow most terminals have PROB30 groups when the best chance for 
impacts will be. No snow is currently indicated in the TAFs at 
KRIW, KLND, KRKS, and KBPI, because the chance is only 20% at 
best. That chance for KRIW and KLND is Saturday afternoon, for 
KRKS is Saturday morning, and for KBPI is Saturday morning 
through Saturday afternoon.

Wind will remain a bit breezy (8-13 knots) through the period. 
Stronger wind will occur at KRKS Saturday afternoon with speeds
around 15 knots and gusts around 25 knots until sunset. 
Frequent mountain obscuration through the period, with some 
improvement Saturday evening near the end of the period. 

Please see the Aviation Weather Center and/or CWSU ZDV and ZLC for 
the latest information on icing and turbulence forecasts.

&&

.RIW WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
Winter Weather Advisory until 11 PM MST this evening for 
WYZ012-014.
